title: Accessing electronic entanglement via photo-assisted two-electron tomography
abstract: Witnessing entanglement between electrons propagating in quantum circuits requires accessing their two-electron coherences, which encode the two-particle quantum correlations generated by Coulomb interactions. Yet, experimental reconstruction of two-electron coherence remains a major challenge. We introduce photo-assisted two-electron tomography, a quantum coherence reconstruction protocol from dc-currents and time-averaged current correlations, routinely measured in electron quantum optics experiments. Driving an energy filter with a small rf tone encodes off-diagonal coherences in the frequency domain into the dc-current response, enabling single-electron tomography without resorting to current-noise measurements. Extending it to two channels, current correlations after two photo-assisted filters reconstruct the two-electron Wigner distribution and isolate its irreducible two-body part. When applied to Coulomb-coupled quantum Hall edge channels, the protocol reveals interaction-induced energy entanglement. Signatures of this entanglement are visible through the violation of an entanglement witness based on Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities, as well as Wigner function negativities, which remain resolved above the thermal background for realistic device parameters. A generalized Franson geometry further extends the approach to intra-channel two-electron coherences. This opens a direct pathway to detect and characterize electronic entanglement in ballistic quantum circuits.

bite.hook: Photo-assisted tomography reconstructs two-electron entanglement in quantum circuits from standard DC current data.
tldr: Introduced a photo-assisted two-electron tomography protocol to reconstruct two-particle quantum coherences.
Modulated energy filters with an RF tone to map quantum coherences into measurable DC currents and current correlations.
Demonstrated that the protocol detects interaction-induced energy entanglement via Cauchy-Schwarz violations and Wigner negativities.
bite.whyItMatters: Proving that flying electrons are entangled in nanoscale circuits has long been hampered by the difficulty of measuring fragile two-particle states. Bypassing complex noise measurements makes it far easier to verify quantum properties in electron-based circuits.
bite.eli5: Electrons traveling down tiny wires interact and get entangled, but reading their joint quantum state usually requires incredibly noisy measurements. By jiggling energy gates with radio waves, researchers convert that hidden quantum information into simple, steady electrical currents.

glossary.eli5Def: A quantum map that describes where two particles are and how they are moving, with negative values proving quantum behavior.

glossary.eli5Def: One-way superhighways for electrons that form along the edges of certain materials in strong magnetic fields.

glossary.shortDef: A mathematical criterion whose violation proves the existence of quantum entanglement.
